sections.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>A column used in a fit</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">4</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">4</text></svg>
sections.figure_alt: A column of two equal entries.
sections.body_md: The squared residual \(\lVert Ax - b \rVert^2\) is a quadratic function of \(x\). Its gradient is \(2 A^T(Ax - b)\), and setting that gradient to zero is the normal equation \(A^T A x = A^T b\). When the columns are independent, \(A^T A\) is invertible and the stationary point is the unique minimizer.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md: Stationarity: \[ A^T A x = A^T b. \] The pseudoinverse of a full-column-rank matrix is \[ A^+ = (A^T A)^{-1} A^T, \] and the minimizer is \(x = A^+ b\). Then \(A^+ A = I\). For a tall matrix, \(A A^+\) is the projection onto the column space rather than the identity. A scalar residual \(ax - b\) has its square stationary at \(x = b/a\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: Take the column \((4, 4)\) and the right-hand side \((8, 14)\). Then \(A^T A = 32\) and \(A^T b = 88\), so the stationary point is \(88/32 = 2.75\). The same number is the pseudoinverse applied to the right-hand side: \(A^+ = (1/8, 1/8)\) and \((1/8) \cdot 8 + (1/8) \cdot 14 = 2.75\). The residual is \((8 - 11, 14 - 11) = (-3, 3)\). It is orthogonal to the column, because \(4 \cdot (-3) + 4 \cdot 3 = 0\). The fit is not exact. The squared length of the residual is 18, which is the value of the quadratic at the stationary point.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: - Replacing \(A^T b\) by \(b\) in the stationarity condition. - Inverting \(AA^T\) for a tall full-column-rank matrix. That larger Gram matrix is singular. - Claiming \(A A^+ = I\) just because \(A^+ A = I\). The first product is a projection when there are more rows than columns. - Expecting the gradient of the squared residual to be \(2A(Ax - b)\) with no transpose.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: A model that is nonlinear in its parameters keeps a residual, but the residual is no longer linear in the unknown, so one normal equation is not the whole fit. A recursive update of the same normal equation takes rows one block at a time. Fitting a circle is the same stationarity idea with a different model.
